question.prompt:
A real-valued function \(f\) has the property that for all real numbers \(a\) and \(b,\)

\[ \begin{gathered} f(a+b)+f(a-b) \\ =2f(a)f(b). \end{gathered} \]

Which one of the following cannot be the value of \(f(1)?\)

solutions.title: Create a square
solutions.explanation:
Choosing equal inputs makes the right side a square, which can give a lower bound without determining the entire function.

First set \(a=b=0\). Then
\[
2f(0)=2f(0)^2,
\]
so \(f(0)\) is either \(0\) or \(1\). Next set \(a=b=\tfrac12\):
\[
f(1)+f(0)=2f\left(\tfrac12\right)^2.
\]
Since the square is nonnegative,
\[
f(1)=2f\left(\tfrac12\right)^2-f(0)\ge -1.
\]
Therefore \(-2\) is impossible.

For completeness, each other listed value is attainable:

| Desired value of \(f(1)\) | A function satisfying the equation |
|---|---|
| \(0\) | \(f(x)=0\) |
| \(1\) | \(f(x)=1\) |
| \(-1\) | \(f(x)=\cos(\pi x)\) |
| \(2\) | \(f(x)=\dfrac{r^x+r^{-x}}2\), where \(r=2+\sqrt3\) |

The constant functions satisfy the equation directly. The cosine example works because the cosine addition and subtraction formulas give
\[
\cos(u+v)+\cos(u-v)=2\cos u\cos v.
\]
For the final example, write \(g(x)=(r^x+r^{-x})/2\). Expanding with the laws of exponents gives
\[
g(a+b)+g(a-b)
=\frac{(r^a+r^{-a})(r^b+r^{-b})}{2}
=2g(a)g(b).
\]
Also, \(r^{-1}=2-\sqrt3\), so \(g(1)=2\).

Thus the value that cannot occur is \(\boxed{-2}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
